- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., sentiment > 0.11) by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low (< 0.06) over 3+ days; model fails to recognize mean reversion.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays downward adjustments by 2–4 days after negative sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment rises sharply (e.g., >0.17) from low base, model overreacts and forecasts higher than true outcome.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts late-period prices (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is positive; apply 1–3% downward adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00 for 3+ days), reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Model underestimates price volatility during sentiment transitions (e.g., 0.06 → 0.17); add 0.5–1.5% buffer for sudden sentiment spikes.
